description: Rookies in software development willing to create an educational game experience from the hardware across the solar system.
summary: PATHFINDERS: Echoes of the Forgotten is an educational 3D adventure and puzzle video game developed in Godot, designed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. The game addresses the “Abandoned but not Forgotten” challenge by transforming the history of abandoned hardware on the Moon and Mars into an interactive, narrative experience for young space enthusiasts. Players control SPARK, an autonomous robot tasked with recovering and restoring historic components from missions such as Surveyor 3, Apollo 12, the LRV-1, Sojourner, Opportunity, and Ingenuity. Through exploration and puzzle-solving mechanics, each restored piece unlocks historical archives that explain the real engineering and science behind these missions. The project fulfills the challenge’s objective by transforming complex technical data into an accessible and exciting narrative, fostering a personal connection with these forgotten explorers and demonstrating that space exploration is also about remembering those who paved the way.
details:
PATHFINDERS: ECHOES OF THE FORGOTTEN is the interactive experience for players which includes exploring the environment, collecting useful objects, solving tasks and getting back the historical components. In each level there are other tasks for players: they need to look around, find the suitable objects for their needs, use them for restoring or reinstalling the missing items. The gameplay of this type allows us teaching players through observing and problem solving.

As we already mentioned the project should be fun and educational, providing the history of space exploration and interesting facts about space technology and science. We decided to combine game with the information and real technical concepts in order to allow players to understand the scientific achievements made during these missions. During the planning of our project we took into account the historical accuracy, educational side, accessibility, player engagement and translation of the technical concepts in the game.

We created the game using Godot with GDScript (96.4%) and GDShader (3.6%). To develop 3D assets we used MagicaVoxel and Blender (plus Python scripting to help us modeling in Blender). For generating code for some 3D assets we used Claude. After this we edited these models in Blender.

Creativity in our game lies in the fact that it uses historically real space technology as the core of the adventure and puzzle games. In contrast to the presentation of technical information in a separate form, here it becomes part of the game when the player interacts with objects, finds out how components function, and applies this knowledge to real space exploration successes.
